English: Due to ballots not being secret, employers and landowners have been able to use their sway over employees and tenants to influence the vote, either by being present themselves or by sending representatives to check on the votes as they are being cast. Small retailers are also concerned not to upset their bigger customers by voting differently from them. To solve these problems, radicals, such as the Chartists, have long campaigned for the a secret ballot to be introduced. With the idea gaining ever more popularity, perhaps it is finally time to pass it into law.

Liberal statesman John Bright has proposed to MP Richard Cobden that, instead of spending money on armaments against a possible French invasion, the British government attempt instead to persuade France to trade freely with Britain. French engineer, statesman and economist Michel Chevalier has spoken out in favor of the treaty and believes that the French monarch can be convinced. By lifting our tariffs, we would increase trade substantially: British manufactured goods will flood into France, whilst French wine, silk and brandy will become widespread in Britain, all at a significantly cheaper price.

The Cobden-Chevalier Treaty is an Anglo-French free trade agreement that has ended tariffs on the main items of trade, including wine, brandy and silk goods from France, and coal, iron and industrial goods from Britain.
